subject: CircuitFold webhook retry loop — triage and SLA coordination
messages:
From: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@circuitfold.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <prao@consultflow.io>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Integration: webhook retry loops resulting in duplicate orders

Hi Rachel —

Quick escalation from our ops team: starting ~15:00 PDT we began seeing a spike of duplicate order events in CircuitFold for customers that receive webhooks from Redwood. We’ve attached a short sample and an error summary.

Symptoms:
- ~4-6x increase in retries for status events for the same order id (IDs in attached webhook_sample.log)
- Duplicate downstream order records created before we can dedupe
- Affected customers: three large merchants in our EU/US pool (listed in PDF)

What we tried on our side:
- Rate-limited incoming webhook processing (reduced throughput, duplicates still persisted)
- Basic request signature check (no anomalies)

As this is impacting revenue events for our customers, we need a coordinated triage and an SLA action plan. Can Redwood confirm whether the retry behavior is from your side (client-side timeouts/resends) or if something in the webhook delivery path is causing repeated deliveries?

Attachments: webhook_sample.log (text), circuitfold_error_summary.pdf (PDF)

Appreciate a quick ack + primary contact for the next 48 hours.

Thanks,
Oliver
Director of Integrations
CircuitFold
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@circuitfold.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration: webhook retry loops resulting in duplicate orders

Oliver —

Thanks for the report and the attached samples. I’m escalating this now and adding Ben (solutions) to lead technical triage and Jordan for partner ops / SLA coordination. We’ll aim to have an initial root-cause assessment and a temporary mitigation plan within 4 hours.

Immediate asks for CircuitFold (if you can):
- Confirm whether you observe multiple identical deliveries (same X-Request-Id) or multiple different request ids for the same order id.
- Any recent deployment or config change on your webhook processing?

Ben — primary owner for triage. Please see the sample logs and summary. If we need to open an SLA amendment or expedited support path, Jordan can lead that thread with CircuitFold.

Oliver — I’ll coordinate periodic updates from our side and set up a short bridge if needed.

-Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@circuitfold.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 01:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Integration: webhook retry loops resulting in duplicate orders

Oliver / Rachel —

I pulled the samples you provided and ran them against delivery logs on our side. Preliminary findings below (quick note: I kept the raw snippets in triage_notes.txt attached).

What I see:
- Redwood delivery attempts show repeated 5xx responses coming from CircuitFold’s ACK endpoint between 15:02–15:12 PDT, after which our worker retried per exponential backoff.
- For some retry attempts, the request payload is identical but our delivery code did not attach an Idempotency-Key header (we rely on downstream services to dedupe based on X-Request-Id).
- CircuitFold appears to be retrying processing when they receive duplicate payloads rather than checking prior X-Request-Id; their consumer returns a 202 in success flows but intermittently returned 502 which triggered Redwood retries.

Temporary mitigations to stop customer impact (recommended order):
1) Redwood: suppress automatic retries to CircuitFold for 30 minutes for the affected account IDs while they roll a quick consumer-side check (config flag I can flip).
2) CircuitFold: add idempotency middleware to the ACK endpoint to dedupe on X-Request-Id or Idempotency-Key.
3) Both: enable request logging with a short TTL so we can compare request ids across the path.

I’ve attached a short triage notes file and a draft escalation_runbook_v1.pdf that documents the temporary suppression step and rollback. If you authorize suppression, we can flip it in ~10 minutes and monitor.

Oliver — can your engineering lead confirm whether they can deploy idempotency middleware within next 24–48 hours? If not, we need a temporary SLA amendment to cover extended mitigation time and credits for duplicate order remediation.

Att: triage_notes.txt, escalation_runbook_v1.pdf

- Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@circuitfold.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration: webhook retry loops resulting in duplicate orders — SLA & MAP

Oliver / team —

Thanks Ben + Rachel for the fast triage. Oliver — we want to make this friction-free on your side. Proposed partner ops next steps and SLA coordination: 

1) Immediate (hour): Redwood will enable suppression of automatic retries for the three affected merchant account IDs. Ben, please proceed when ready and post a status update to this thread.
2) Short-term (24–48 hours): CircuitFold to deploy idempotency middleware or equivalent dedupe check. If CircuitFold needs more time, we’ll accept a staged rollout with a temporary 72-hour exception window.
3) SLA amendment: I’ve attached a draft SLA_amendment_draft.docx that adds a remediation credit table and an expedited support lane for P1 partner incidents. Please review and send any redlines by end of day Monday.
4) Mutual action plan (MAP): I created a short MAP doc — link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/map/CF-integration-triage-2026 (internal). If you want a shared Google Drive link for CircuitFold, we can provision one.

Ownership:
- Redwood ops/triage lead: Ben Carter
- Redwood partner ops: Jordan Blake (me) — SLA negotiation / credit discussion
- CircuitFold engineering lead: Oliver Shaw (please confirm or give alternate)

If CircuitFold confirms the 24–48 deploy timeline we’ll avoid credits and aim to restore normal traffic without customer impact. If not, we’ll start the SLA amendment process.

Attachments: SLA_amendment_draft.docx

Jordan Blake
Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
